beta.notes:
Native Plex client for MiSTer. Built for CRTs at 480i over Component, RGB, S-Video or Composite, with 480p on HDMI.

Beta access. This is a paid early-access build. Install and browsing work without a code. Playback needs the code from the MisterZine Patreon post. Stable releases will be free and codeless.

New in beta.12
- No more long black screen while a video starts. The title strip stays up and an amber dot slides back and forth in the middle of the screen until the first frame appears. The same dot shows while a new audio or subtitle track comes up, and while the player restarts a stream after a network hiccup.
- Down closes the playback controls. On the timeline it first steps down to the buttons, and a scrub you just made still goes through.
- Back no longer stops the video by accident. For a second after the controls, the seek bar, a track list or the skip button go away, Back does nothing, so a second press meant for them is harmless.
- The screen dims to a quarter after three minutes in the menus or on a paused video, to spare CRTs (and OLED TVs over HDMI) from a still picture. Any button brings it back and does nothing else, so OK on a paused video only wakes the screen.
- Opening Plex right after switching the MiSTer on no longer fails with "Cannot reach the server". For the first minute it keeps trying quietly, showing "Connecting to" your server and what it is waiting for: the network, the clock or an answer.

Everything from beta.11 is included.

Requirements
- Networked MiSTer on current MiSTer Linux
- 250 MB free on the SD card
- Plex account with a server that can transcode

Install
1. Download the Beta installer below and put it in the SD card's Scripts folder.
2. Run it from Scripts.
3. Follow the sign-in screen at plex.tv/link.

Already on an earlier beta: open Options > Updates in the app and install from there.

NTSC 480i only; PAL isn't supported yet.

This is unstable beta software. It talks to your real Plex account: playback, watched marks and resume points change your library, and a bug could change them wrongly. Use it at your own risk; no responsibility is taken for what it does to your library or your MiSTer.
